headline: ⏰ NOT ONE FUTURE SHOWING IS BOOKED ON ANY LISTING, NOTHING NEW HAS BEEN SCHEDULED IN NINETY-ONE HOURS, AND THE ONLY THING THAT ARRIVED OVERNIGHT WAS A SECOND “too high” ON 2368 RIDGE TRAIL — which makes today's most valuable half-hour the two calls nobody is chasing: the “VERY interested” buyer at 821 Martinwood, ten days unanswered, and Amy G. at 355 Comanche, whose buyers put the house at the top of their list six days ago and who is still waiting to hear why the basement lights would not come on.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 AMY G. OF ETHOS INTERNATIONAL filed Saturday at 11:24 PM off that afternoon's 1:00 PM tour: interested — YES, buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the TOP OF THEIR LIST. She left both price fields blank, which on this listing is now the fifth consecutive read that declined to argue the number.
hotSignals.action: ☎️ CALL HER — day six, and this is a returned call rather than a cold approach: she is the same agent who phoned from inside the house mid-showing. Two things to carry: answer the basement-lights question she raised in the same form, and ask directly where the house sits against whatever else her buyers are touring this week. ⛔ Call rather than write — the co-op mail lane is a deliberate hold, day twelve unruled.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 AMBER G. OF KELLER WILLIAMS HOOVER: interested — YES, priced right — JUST RIGHT, staging five of five. This remains the single strongest pricing evidence anywhere in the book and the cleanest confirmation that the 8/5 cut did its job.
hotSignals.action: ☎️ Eight days out, so treat this as a status check rather than a fresh lead — are her buyers still live, and did anything specific push them elsewhere? ⭐ Her form is also the receipt to quote to the seller the next time price comes up: do not reopen the number.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 WANDA W. OF MILLENNIUM HOMES answered the interest question with the single word “Very” and rated the experience at the top. Two other agents toured within seventy minutes of her and both passed — so the interest here is one clear voice, not a crowd.
hotSignals.action: 🔴 TEN DAYS UNWORKED AND THIS IS THE CHEAPEST CONTRACT ON THE WHOLE BOARD. At $184K a very-interested buyer is a two-week close, not a six-week one. ☎️ One call: are they still looking, and what would it take? Nothing on this board has a better effort-to-outcome ratio.

upcoming: ⏰ THU 8/20, 3:00 PM — 5167 LAKE CREST CIR closes at the closing attorney's office. Not a ShowingTime event, but it is the nearest hard date on the board and the largest number closing this month. ⚠️ Still no clear-to-close on any lane after a fourth independent search, and the city inspector's sign-off is now scheduled onto closing morning itself.
📅 SAT 8/30 — 833 MADISON LN goes live. Newly tracked as of last night; nothing is booked on it yet because it is not on the market yet.

📤 OVERDUE RATHER THAN UPCOMING — 225 WILLOW POINT was promised a same-day launch at 2:40 PM yesterday and did not go live. The photographs are ready and the agreement is executed; until the entry is made there is nothing for ShowingTime to book.

📭 NO SHOWINGS BOOKED ANYWHERE, AND NOTHING NEW HAS BEEN SCHEDULED SINCE SATURDAY AFTERNOON — ninety-one hours. There is not one future showing, walk-through, inspection or appraisal confirmed on any listing. ⭐ Read it honestly: a silent feed in mid-August across seven actives is a marketing problem rather than a bad-luck week, and the only listing still producing any signal at all is the $295K one.

listings.note: ⭐ THE PRICING QUESTION IS SETTLED AND SHOULD NOT BE REOPENED WITH THIS SELLER. Every read that ever said TOO HIGH was filed while the ask was $299,000; the cut went live 8/5. Five consecutive reads since and not one argued the number — a $4,000 experiment that worked. 🔴 THE LIVE ITEM IS THE BASEMENT LIGHTS, raised by the hottest agent on the file and unanswered since Saturday. 🔴 Two agents who filed TOO HIGH at the OLD price still do not know it moved — both chips overdue since 8/8, now eleven days.

listings.status: 📉 ACTIVE — three tours in ten days, and the one read that came back says the number is still too high

feedback.agent: Drew T. · Keller Williams Realty Vestavia
feedback.note: NEW overnight. Off the Sat 8/15 4:00 PM tour: interested — No, priced — TOO HIGH. Price-recommendation, staging and comment fields all left blank, so he named no number he WOULD pay.

gaps: Mon 8/10 2:00 PM tour — nothing filed, nine days

listings.note: ⚠️ THIS IS THE SECOND INDEPENDENT TOO-HIGH READ ON THIS ADDRESS, AND THE ASK HAS ALREADY COME DOWN FROM $559,000. ⭐ But read the shape rather than the one form: three tours in ten days and two of the three filed nothing at all. A blank price-recommendation is a softer signal than a real counter — the more useful number here is that two thirds of the people who walked it never said why they passed. 📇 The seller side on this file is an institutional owner, so feedback routes to a portfolio mailbox rather than a person.

Ten days later there is no recorded reply to any of the three. ⭐ At this price point a very-interested buyer is a two-week close — this is the cheapest contract available anywhere and it is aging for no reason.

feedback.note: Interested — No, but priced JUST RIGHT. A pass on fit rather than on price, filed the same day as the inspection.

listings.note: ✅ THE HOUSE HALF IS DONE — the seller signed the inspection-contingency-removal addendum at 12:28 PM yesterday and every repair item is agreed. 🔴 THE OPEN ITEM IS NO LONGER A SHOWING QUESTION: the other side raised a doubt that a prior deed may never have been recorded, which is a title defect, and it surfaced four minutes before that addendum was signed. Close is 9/14, so there is room — but title problems get expensive when they are left to the last fortnight.

listings.note: 🎉 The longest runway on the board and nothing owed this week. ⭐ One note that belongs to marketing rather than the deal: the proof-post built off this listing is still queued and unpublished alongside two others.

listings.note: ✅ BOTH GATES ARE BEHIND IT — inspection 8/5, appraisal 8/7, close holding at 8/28. ⭐ Nine days out with nothing outstanding on the file, which makes the only open item a human one: the seller has been waiting on a call, and this is the week to make it.

listings.status: ⏰ CLOSES TOMORROW 3:00 PM — preliminary title policy in hand, still no clear-to-close on any lane
listings.note: ⏰ ONE DAY OUT AND A FOURTH INDEPENDENT SEARCH FOUND THE SAME NOTHING. ✅ Verified and good: preliminary title policy delivered, appraisal clean, repair addendum executed, septic run 8/4. ⚠️ The wrong-way item: the city inspector's sign-off sits on closing morning — and the message that says so opens on a different property and never names this one, so the match rests on circumstantial legs rather than anyone's words. Two texts settle it.

Will get it on the market today.” Three independent checks say it did not go live. ⭐ Nothing can be booked on a listing that is not on the market — this is the cheapest repair available today.

listings.note: 🛑 Listed here only because two tours inside the fourteen-day window still sit unanswered and one of them was a SECOND showing by the same buyer. ⭐ Worth one honest look before it is filed away: this listing carried a written offer on 8/4 and a second showing on 8/13, and it still expired — that sequence is the most instructive thing on this page.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 THREE ASKS AND TWENTY-NINE DAYS OF SILENCE — 7/21, 7/22 and 7/23 from the RealtySouth Inverness listing side after the 7/21 1:00 PM tour. ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE THAT COSTS SOMETHING REAL, and the cost is not the courtesy — it is that the honest written answer IS the counter on the largest number on the board, roughly $36K of GCI. The listing side has asked repeatedly to be moved forward; a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal. Twenty minutes of writing moves it. ⚠️ The appraisal figure the buyer cited as far under ask is single-sourced from him — do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value.

⏰ TWO FEEDBACK REQUESTS, 7/31 and 8/1, from the Keller Williams Hoover listing side. The listing went from CONTINGENT to EXPIRED between the two notices, so the ask is stale — but a one-line courtesy reply costs nothing, and this is a Lake Crest-subdivision agent you may well meet at a closing table tomorrow.
